description: Imports Intercom customer-support data (contacts, companies, conversations and their parts, tickets, tags, teams, admins, segments and data attributes) from the Intercom REST API.

spec.apiVersionPinning: request header `Intercom-Version`, sent on every request; value comes from endpoint config `advanced.api_version` (default "2.11", pattern ^\d+\.\d+$)

configFields.name: credentials.credentials_title
configFields.description: Discriminator selecting the auth variant: "Private App Credentials" or "OAuth Credentials".

configFields.name: credentials.access_token
configFields.description: Intercom access token. Present in both credential variants.

configFields.name: start_date
configFields.description: UTC date/time YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ; defaults to 30 days before now. Seeds the incremental cursor of every incremental binding.

configFields.name: advanced.window_size
configFields.description: Window size in days for date-windowed incremental streams (contacts). Default 5, must be > 0.

configFields.name: advanced.use_companies_list_endpoint
configFields.description: Default false. When true, companies and company_segments enumerate companies via POST /companies/list (page-number pagination, ~10k cap); when false they use GET /companies/scroll.

configFields.name: advanced.search_page_size
configFields.description: per_page for the search endpoints (contacts, tickets, conversations, conversation_parts). Default and maximum 150.

configFields.name: advanced.api_version
configFields.description: Value of the Intercom-Version header. Default "2.11".

configFields.name: interval
configFields.description: ISO-8601 duration between updates for this resource; every binding ships with PT5M.

pathPlaceholders.conversation_id: id of each conversation returned by the parent POST /conversations/search traversal (same body_cursor paginator as the `conversations` stream); fetched with at most 15 concurrent requests, and a 404 is treated as a deleted conversation and skipped

pathPlaceholders.company_id: id of each company from the parent companies traversal (GET /companies/scroll by default, POST /companies/list when advanced.use_companies_list_endpoint is true); all ids are buffered before any segment request is issued, and a 404 is treated as a deleted company and skipped

authTierRationale: The connector offers two mutually exclusive credential variants discriminated by `credentials_title`. The easiest is "Private App Credentials" (estuary_cdk AccessToken): the user pastes a single Intercom access token, which the CDK TokenSource sends verbatim as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` — one self-serve secret, T1_SIMPLE. The alternative is `LongLivedClientCredentialsOAuth2Credentials` for provider "intercom", which standalone requires the user to register their own Intercom OAuth app (client_id + client_secret) AND supply a long-lived access_token, so it is at least T2 and, because of the extra pre-obtained token, effectively T3. Estuary's hosted control plane performs the authorization_code exchange (authUrlTemplate https://app.intercom.com/oauth, accessTokenUrlTemplate https://api.intercom.io/auth/eagle/token, token read from response pointer /token) on the user's behalf, but the standalone tier is what is recorded. Overall = the easiest mode = T1_SIMPLE.

unionMisfits.description: companies and company_segments have TWO mutually exclusive parent-traversal shapes selected at runtime by the endpoint-config boolean advanced.use_companies_list_endpoint. Default (false): GET /companies/scroll with an opaque `scroll_param` query cursor echoed from the response envelope field `scroll_param`, terminating when `data` is empty, guarded by a process-global asyncio lock because Intercom permits only one scroll per workspace (a concurrent scroll yields HTTP 400 'scroll already exists for this workspace'). When true: POST /companies/list with page-number pagination (query params per_page=60, page=1..pages.total_pages), which Intercom hard-caps at ~10,000 companies and then returns HTTP 400 'page limit reached, please use scroll API' — the connector swallows that error and simply stops, silently truncating. The Paginator union has no way to express a config-conditional choice between two paginators, nor the single-flight constraint. Only the default (scroll) mode is emitted above.

cases.hardCap: ~10000 records, then HTTP 400 'page limit reached, please use scroll API' is caught and pagination stops

unionMisfits.description: Incremental filtering for the three search streams is not a query parameter and does not fit `incrementalParam`. It is a nested boolean query tree in the JSON POST body over the `updated_at` field with unix-second values, plus a `sort` block. contacts uses `(updated_at > lower AND updated_at < upper) OR (updated_at = lower OR updated_at = upper)` sorted DESC (Intercom filters contacts by date, not exact timestamp) and stops paginating early once a record older than the window start is seen; tickets/conversations use `updated_at > lower AND updated_at <= upper` sorted ascending. contacts additionally windows the request range into `advanced.window_size`-day chunks. segments, companies and company_segments send no server-side time filter at all and filter `updated_at` purely client-side.

Both are child streams: the records they emit come from an unpaginated per-parent sub-request, while all pagination happens on the parent traversal. The PullSpec has no field for 'parent stream' — the parent paginator is only representable by prose inside pathPlaceholders. conversation_parts additionally derives its incremental cursor entirely from the parent conversations sweep (it re-uses fetch_conversations and forwards its checkpoints).

child.notFoundPolicy: skip on 404 (parent deleted between listing and fetch)

unionMisfits.description: Recorded as {"type":"none"} because the response model forbids extra fields and has no pagination object, but the connector author notes in a code comment that Intercom's docs say the /segments response MAY contain a pagination object that they never observed. If it does appear on a large workspace the connector will hard-fail on validation rather than silently truncate — so 'none' is safe here, but it is an unverified assumption, not a documented API guarantee.

proposedShape.failureMode: strict model validation error rather than silent truncation

abstained.streams[6].pull.backfill: There is no separate backfill leg. Every incremental binding is opened with fetch_changes only (no fetch_page), seeded from config.start_date; the historical sweep and the ongoing sweep are the same code path. Recorded under `incremental` rather than invented as a distinct backfill PullSpec.
abstained.streams[*].pull.incremental.incrementalP: Null for every stream. No stream sends a time filter as a query parameter. contacts/tickets/conversations express it as a nested boolean query object in the POST body (see unionMisfits[1]); segments/companies/company_segments do no server-side filtering at all. Forcing a {param, format} value here would be wrong.
abstained.streams[11].pull.incremental.paginator (: Only the DEFAULT mode (GET /companies/scroll, advanced.use_companies_list_endpoint=false) is emitted. When the flag is true the connector instead uses POST /companies/list with page-number pagination (per_page=60, page from 1 until page >= pages.total_pages). A single Paginator value cannot express both; the alternate is recorded in unionMisfits[0] rather than guessed into the stream. Note the repo's own config.yaml test fixture sets use_companies_list_endpoint: true, i.e. the tested mode is NOT the default mode.
abstained.streams[12].pull.incremental.paginator (: Emitted as {type: none} because the per-company GET /companies/{id}/segments request is genuinely unpaginated; the dual-mode pagination described in unionMisfits[0] belongs to the parent company traversal, which the PullSpec shape cannot carry.
abstained.streams[10].pull.incremental.paginator (: Emitted as {type: none} on the strength of the observed response model, but the connector author explicitly records that Intercom's docs claim a pagination object may exist and they could not reproduce it. See unionMisfits[3]. Failure mode if it exists is a hard validation error, not silent truncation.
abstained.execution.continuity: Null. mode is poll over a third-party HTTP API; no server-side artifacts are created on the customer's side and nothing accrues between polls. The single exception is the /companies/scroll cursor, which Intercom scopes one-per-workspace and expires after roughly one minute — but it is created and consumed entirely inside one fetch call and is not held across cron ticks, so it is not a continuity artifact. (The connector's own comment at api.py:614-615 says it buffers company ids specifically to avoid holding the scroll open longer than necessary.)
abstained.streams[*].writeDisposition: Full-refresh bindings are marked snapshot_with_tombstone because the CDK's SnapshotResource docstring states the /_meta/row_id key exists for deletion inference; the actual tombstone emission lives in CDK snapshot-subtask code that was not read line by line. Incremental bindings are `merge` on the strength of key=["/id"] plus an updated_at cursor; no delete detection exists for them.
abstained.discovery: Null: streamMode is static. The 13 bindings are hard-coded in five module-level lists in resources.py; nothing is read from the customer's account to build the stream list. Field-level schemas are inferred at runtime (schema_inference=True), but that is schema inference, not stream discovery.
